evaluations.label: A
errors: Recap lists a 'preview button'; the transcript says 'previous channel button'

Left/right-handed question: 'The group did not document a detailed resolution' understates it; the PM said it works for both hands and lighted buttons help, and the UI designer accepted ('Okay. Maybe.')
Places the wheel-keeping decision at [11:04]; at that point the PM only said it 'maybe' would be an advantage; the decision came at about 15:54
strengths: Captures key numbers: wheel sensor 50x a push button, €12 cost ceiling
Covers the voice-recognition chip email and says clearly that no decision was made to add voice
Records the banana/yellow/wheel-on-top decision, the spongy cover, the standard battery and chip, and the industrial + UI designer collaboration
Timestamps and a clear structure with a summary up top
weaknesses: The Action items section is empty even though the assignments appear in the body
Some repetition (the 50x fact appears twice; the wheel being kept is stated several times)
The plastic cover outcome and the lighting outcome are left vague

evaluations.label: B
errors: 'Heart-shaped core with spongy cover suggested'; the PM said 'odd shaped, with a spongy cover'
UI designer named 'UL Hazred'; the name given was Abdul al-Hasred
'Light turns on with motion sensor' is stated as fact; it was only debated and not decided
Lists previous-meeting items under 'Simple remote interface confirmed' as if they were decided in this meeting
Invented action items such as 'Assess cost implications of wheel sensor', 'Facilitate discussion on wheel sensor necessity' and 'Provide meeting notes in shared folder (00:00)'
'Banana shape proposed' understates it; the banana was adopted as the decision
strengths: Includes the 50x cost and the €12 budget
Covers the plastic-cover debate and the left/right-hand discussion
Has an explicit per-person action list that includes the designers' collaboration and the email instructions
weaknesses: Leaves out the voice-recognition chip email entirely
Never states clearly that the wheel was kept despite its cost, or that the standard battery and chip were confirmed
Action items are padded with speculative tasks

evaluations.label: C
errors: 'Backlit buttons confirmed' is a bit strong; lighting was debated and only assumed later
'hard internal structure' adds 'hard', which is not in the transcript
Next steps split the work ('Industrial designer to produce final design', 'UI designer to finalize layout'); the PM actually asked both to work together and did not split it this way
strengths: Clear recap of the previous meeting's decisions
Component decisions are explicit: standard battery, chip, wheel kept despite ~50x cost, €12 ceiling
Voice chip handled correctly as deferred
Banana design captured fully: yellow, company colors, easy to find, wheel on top, buttons on the side, spongy cover, left/right-hand resolution
Next steps are specific and include the check against user requirements
weaknesses: Next steps lean toward inferred owners
Plastic cover outcome described as 'reconsidered' rather than as an explicit decision

evaluations.label: D
errors: 'IS1001c remote control' is a label that never appears in the transcript
'backlit buttons that activate upon movement' is presented as a spec; motion activation was debated and not decided
'arched internal structure for component mounting' is invented ('arched' was never said)
'tactile appeal' as a reason for the spongy material is unsupported
Uses 'UIZ' and generic 'Speaker 1-4' labels inconsistently with the role names
'Action Items (none)' contradicts the PM assigning the industrial and UI designers to work together on the prototype
strengths: A good list of open questions (voice chip adaptation, motion sensor cost against €12, button feel through the sponge)
Covers the 50x cost, the €12 budget, the plastic cover rejection, the push-down wheel and the banana/yellow decision
The outline gives a readable chronological flow
weaknesses: Mixes speaker numbers and role abbreviations, which is confusing
Repeats content between the summary and the outline
Wheel-on-top and buttons-on-side placement is only briefly covered

rationale: C is the most accurate and complete. It records the component decisions, the voice chip deferral, the banana design details and concrete next steps, with only minor overstatements. A is accurate and well sourced but leaves its Action items section empty and has a small 'preview button' slip. D covers most topics and lists open questions well, but it states the motion-activated light as decided, invents details ('IS1001c', 'arched' structure) and says there are no action items. B has a clear factual error ('heart-shaped'), a garbled name, padded and invented action items, and it leaves out the voice chip discussion.
